candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — calcium and bone-health teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Explain calcium's ongoing role in bone structure and maintenance and the importance of meeting age-appropriate recommended intake rather than routinely exceeding it.

options.A: Calcium has little role in adult bone because skeletal mineralization is complete by early adulthood
options.B: Calcium intake should routinely exceed recommended amounts because more calcium consistently prevents fractures in all adults
options.C: Adequate vitamin D and physical activity make calcium intake unnecessary for bone maintenance
options.D: Calcium is a major structural component of bone, and intake should generally meet age- and sex-appropriate recommendations

candidate.rationale: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements guidance states that calcium makes up much of the structure of bones and that bone undergoes continuous remodeling throughout life. Recommended calcium intake varies by age and sex; for adults, recommended amounts are based largely on bone maintenance and calcium balance. Routine intake above recommended amounts is not supported as a universal fracture-prevention strategy and can carry risks. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Calcium is a major structural component of bone; bone remodels continuously; recommended intakes vary by age/sex and are designed in adults to support bone maintenance and calcium balance.
